title: The Sunday post, issue 2
pageTitle: Duncan’s First Win, Tiger’s Return & a Blind-Hole Rule | SundayStroke
summary: Duncan wins at her 222nd try, Tiger returns in December, and a rule for blind tee shots.
leadText: The rules say nobody may stand out on a blind hole as your target, so the line is yours to pick. Here is a swing before and after Tracer drew the ball’s flight onto the video: film your tee shot on a blind hole and watch its flight on your own video.

items.headline: Duncan wins at the 222nd try
items.body: Lindy Duncan won The Annika on Sunday 15 November at 16 under, two ahead of Hye-Jin Choi, for her first LPGA Tour title in her 222nd start. At 35, she is the tour’s oldest first-time winner since 2008.

items.headline: Tiger is back in December
items.body: Tiger Woods, 50, is in the 20-man field for the Hero World Challenge at Albany Golf Club in New Providence on 3–6 December. He has not played on the PGA Tour since missing the cut at the 2024 Open.

items.headline: No human markers on blind holes
items.body: Under Rule 10.2b, a playing partner may not stand out on a blind hole as a target while you hit, though they can point out a tree or other object that shows the line. Going ahead purely to watch where the balls finish is fine.

items.headline: October’s players give back
items.body: The PDGA’s October pledge, a gift for every player entry in a gender-based division at C-tier and higher events, counted 3,467 entries, so Throw Pink gets more than last year. It is the third year in a row the October fundraiser has gone to Throw Pink.
